enunciado: “If it ___ tomorrow, I will stay home.”
explicacion:
✔ *If it rains tomorrow, I will stay home.*

First conditional: if + present simple, will + verb. Real future possibility.

enunciado: “If I ___ you, I would accept that job offer.”
explicacion:
✔ *If I were you, I would accept that job offer.*

Second conditional for advice: If I were you… We use were for all persons.

enunciado: “If I won the lottery, I ___ around the world.”
explicacion:
✔ *If I won the lottery, I would travel around the world.*

Second conditional: if + past simple, would + verb. Imaginary situation.

enunciado: “If we had left earlier, we ___ late.”
explicacion:
✔ *If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have been late.*

Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle. A past that didn't happen.

enunciado: “If I ___ harder, I would have passed the exam.”
explicacion:
✔ *If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.*

Third conditional: the if-clause takes the past perfect (had + participle).

enunciado: “___ you hurry, you will be late.”
explicacion:
✔ *Unless you hurry, you will be late.*

Unless = if not. Unless you hurry = if you don't hurry.

enunciado: Which conditional expresses a regret about the past?
explicacion: Third conditional: regrets, criticism, missed opportunities.

enunciado: “What ___ you do if you had more free time?”
explicacion:
✔ *What would you do if you had more free time?*

Second conditional question: What would you do if + past simple?

enunciado: “If I had saved more money, I ___ bought a car.”
explicacion:
✔ *If I had saved more money, I could have bought a car.*

Could have / might have can replace would have in the third conditional.

enunciado: “If my friend visits, we ___ go to a concert.”
explicacion:
✔ *If my friend visits, we might go to a concert.*

First conditional can use might instead of will for a less certain result.

enunciado: “If I hadn't been nervous, I ___ better in the interview.”
explicacion:
✔ *If I hadn't been nervous, I would have done better in the interview.*

Third conditional, negative if-clause: if + hadn't + participle, would have + participle.
